Kennedy Center Announces 2026 Honors: Mamet, Anka, Garcia Among Recipients

The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts has officially announced its 2026 slate of honorees. The prestigious ceremony will take place for the first time at the Capital One Arena on December 7.

Confirmed Honorees

The following five artists will receive the honor:

  • Paul Anka: The legendary singer-songwriter behind hits like "Diana" and "My Way."
  • David Foster: A 16-time Grammy winning composer who helped launch the careers of Celine Dion and Michael Bublé.
  • Andy Garcia: An Oscar-nominated actor whose credits include "The Godfather: Part III" and "Ocean’s Eleven."
  • David Mamet: The Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, screenwriter, director, and author behind "Glengarry Glen Ross" and "Oleanna."
  • Barbara Mandrell: A country singer best known for "I’ve Been Loving You Too Long" and "(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don’t Want to Be Right."

Ceremony Details and Unknowns

The announcement was made surprisingly late, as honorees are typically revealed between July and September.

  • Host: Not yet announced.
  • Broadcast Partner: Not yet announced. CBS historically aired the event every year since its inception in 1978, but the network’s broadcast rights expired in 2025.

Institutional Controversies

The announcement comes amid ongoing political drama surrounding the institution, which has historically avoided partisan issues.

  • Building Renaming: The center’s board, handpicked by Chairman Donald Trump, voted in December 2025 to add his name to the building. A federal judge ruled in May that only Congress can rename the building, causing Trump's name to come down in June. After the judge blocked another attempt in September, the board voted to close the center, citing structural deterioration.
  • Renovations: Trump has stated renovations will not begin unless a higher court allows his name to return, warning the building could otherwise end up "ripped down." His Justice Department has backed the President, arguing the center faces financial and physical collapse without his name.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers seeking to verify this information should consult the original Variety announcement at variety.com and the official Kennedy Center website. Because the ceremony lacks a host and broadcast partner, and faces potential closure, fans are advised to monitor official announcements for any updates regarding the event's format and continuation. Past honorees include Aretha Franklin, Paul McCartney, Meryl Streep, Steven Spielberg, Bruce Springsteen, Dolly Parton, Led Zeppelin, and Sidney Poitier.
